Guidance & outlook: EBITDA however, declined to INR34 crores in FY26 compared to INR43 crores in FY25 due to a decline in H1 of FY26 which was at INR10 crores.
We expect revenue booking of about INR100 crores in the existing orders in FY27 and the remaining amount in FY28.
We are targeting INR20 crores to INR30 crores in sales from this division in FY27, supported by developmental or export orders in hand and encouraging momentum in the domestic market.
Growth & demand: Total annual revenue stood at INR329 crores in second half of the year and INR 549 crores for the whole year, representing nearly 50% growth both sequentially and on a full-year basis.
While we achieved 25% growth in volume, revenue from CRGO processing increased by only 10% in the whole year.
Given our existing resources and execution bandwidth, we believe we are positioned to handle additional orders of up to INR500 crores alongside our current order book.
Margins & costs: Raw material prices fell by a staggering 30% to 35% from March 2025 to March 2026, causing extreme volatility in the supply chain.

With an installed capacity of close to 24,000 metric tonnes per annum, we are currently operating at a monthly capacity utilization of about 65%, with the most hope for ramping up in power transformer cores.
So, we believe that -- I mean I have always guided in the past that 10% to 12% EBITDA margin is a good stable level if raw material prices or the overall market is stable.
Capex & expansion: We have completed all the CapEx-related activities in manufacturing as planned and on time in the last two fiscal years, amounting to about INR30 crores, which has the peak potential of manufacturing sales of INR500 crores to INR600 crores at the prevailing price levels and INR700 crores to INR800 crores if CRGO prices bounce back to previous levels.
We do not have major capacity expansion plans in FY27 as our focus will be on improving utilization across capacities.
So, capacity utilization comes out to be about 65%.
Balance sheet & cash: In total, the company generated a cash flow from operations of INR30.1 crores as compared to a negative INR33.87 crores in the previous year due to a prudent capital allocation approach.
The overall receivables increased to INR190 crores in the year versus INR78 crores in FY25, resulting from a spike in EPC sales in the last two months of the financial year.
So, out of the trade receivables of INR190 crores, our receivables in the EPC business is to the tune of INR118 crores.
Risks & challenges: While the entire year remained more challenging than anticipated, we laid the foundation for multiple long-term growth drivers for the company.
The annual decline in profits resulted mainly from continued volatility in the CRGO business.
Excessive imports from China caused multiple sharp declines in raw material prices, creating an oversupply in the market and difficulties in planning.
